reason: Verbatim quote; Schneider J's construction of s.325 that the summary obstruction procedure requires obstruction at or shortly after delivery of possession is the ratio dismissing the petition.
Statement and quote reproduce the headnote holding verbatim; the court construed s.287 to hold a mortgage-decree purchaser gets delivery of possession only against a defendant in the mortgage action.

The proposition is only Sinnetamby J's individual view (headnoted 'Per SINNETAMBY, J.') and Basnayake CJ held the opposite (the Crown cannot claim immunity from its laches), so it is not the court's ratio or decision.

Verbatim holding; the court construed s.5 (read with s.217(G) and s.62 of the Courts Ordinance) to hold a civil court has jurisdiction to make a decree declaring a status, the ratio rejecting the jurisdiction objection.
The statement is an accurate ratio, but the Board grounded concealed fraud in equity and precedent, not in the tagged statute section, so the statute attribution is unsupported.

Verbatim rule from the headnote; the court construed s.540 to hold an administrator cannot begin prescribing against the heirs until he completes the administration, the ratio rejecting the prescription plea.
Verbatim holding; the ratio dismissing the appeal is that the Bank is not liable for the debtor's loss from parate execution absent negligence.
Verbatim headnote rule; the ratio allowing the appeal is that the plaintiff failed to prove ten years' adverse possession from ouster for the alleged divided portion.

The rule that a wife living apart by consent cannot alienate community property is an accurate ratio supported verbatim, but the court rested it on Roman-Dutch authority, not the tagged statute section.
Verbatim holding of Basnayake J construing s.8(c) of the Rent Restriction Ordinance; only the landlord's reasonable requirement matters, the ratio allowing the landlord's appeal.
Accurate statement of the prescription rule and its exception in the court's own words; the court construed s.362 to hold the action time-barred because the cause of action arose at the tort.
Verbatim principle applied by the court, with the quote confirming delegation outside recognized limits is void, to hold the trustee's purported delegation void and dismiss the action.

Accurate ratio supported verbatim (receipt of a writ operates as seizure of already-sequestered goods), but it rests on ss.236/660/661, not the tagged s.247, which is merely the claimant-action section.
